description: Core data model: Pipe entity (Kanban board) with ordered Phases, labels, and start form fields
ui_details: Confirmed (Iteration 3, live test): Início dashboard's tabbed Pipes/Databases grid — the 'Criar pipe' (+) tile opens a template-gallery side modal (search box + 'Categorias de processos' left rail of industry categories + a grid of 'AI Studio' template cards) with two bottom CTAs: 'Criar pipe do zero' and 'Criar com IA'. Clicking 'Criar pipe do zero' opens a second, minimal modal on top: a single 'Nome do pipe' text input, 'Criar pipe' submit button disabled until non-empty — same two-step shape as feature-005's Database Table create flow (template gallery is Database's equivalent-less; Database create is name-only from the start). Submitting redirects straight to the new pipe's Kanban board at /pipes/:id. Back on Início, the pipe grid card shows the pipe's icon glyph in a colored square, name, and 'N cards' count.
behavior: A Pipe has id, uuid, name, color, users_count, cards_count, opened_cards_count. Has many ordered Phases, Labels ({id,name,color}), start_form_fields, and members ({user{id,email}, role_name}). CONFIRMED: every pipe created via 'Criar pipe do zero' auto-provisions the SAME 3-phase starter template — Caixa de entrada (done=false), Fazendo (done=false), Concluído (done=true) — with cards_count=0 in each phase; this matches the org's pre-existing 'Purchase Requests' pipe, confirming it's a fixed default template rather than a blank pipe. CONFIRMED: color is server-assigned at creation (no color picker in either creation modal, and it's not derived from the name — two pipes created back-to-back got a teal swatch and a green swatch respectively); color is user-editable afterward via Configurações do pipe (feature-014), so it's a mutable field with a system-chosen initial value, not an immutable hash of the name. NOTE: the live app's frontend talks to a single batched POST https://app.pipefy.com/internal_api endpoint rather than discrete REST routes per action — irrelevant to the clone's own API design (which must expose conventional REST/JSON routes per spec-build.md), but confirms there is no literal endpoint shape to mirror, only UI-observed behavior.
data_model: pipes: id, uuid, name, color (server-assigned on create, user-editable after), org_id (fk), cards_count (derived), opened_cards_count (derived). labels: id, pipe_id (fk), name, color. Pipe creation is a single required field (name) — all other fields (color, the 3 default phases) are server-populated side effects of the create action, not user input.

description: Core data model: Card entity — the unit of work moving through a Pipe's phases, holding Card Field Values
ui_details: Confirmed (Iteration 3, live test): Kanban 'Criar novo card' / a phase column's '+' is BLOCKED until the pipe's start form has ≥1 field — with an empty start form both open a 'Compartilhar formulário' promo modal instead of a create form. Once the start form has a field, the same buttons open an inline popover create-form (title + fields + 'Criar novo card' submit); required-field validation shows a red border + 'deve ser informado' inline, no toast, submit blocked. On success: toast 'Card criado com sucesso. Para abri-lo, clique aqui' + card appears at top of its phase column titled with the first field's submitted value. Card detail view (3 columns): LEFT = title, quick actions (Adicionar responsável/Vencimento/Adicionar etiquetas), tab strip (Form/Atividades/Anexos/Checklists/Comentários/Email/PDF/+), read-only 'Formulário Inicial' section (creator + relative timestamp + submitted field values), 'Histórico' phase-transition timeline, 'Editar visualização do card' link. MIDDLE = 'Fase atual' badge + gear (phase settings) + Compartilhar, then the current phase's own fields as a live autosave-on-blur form (no save button; no toast on this particular autosave). RIGHT = 'Mover card para fase' one-click button naming the next phase, 'Configurar mover cards', 'Mover cards com IA'. Cards in a done:true phase render a checkmark + '<N>min' badge and dimmed title text.
behavior: A Card has id, title, done (bool), updated_at, belongs to a current phase, and has many field values ({name, value, filled_at, field}). Cards move between phases (drag-and-drop on Kanban, or the detail view's quick-mover button); moving a card fires toast 'Card movido com sucesso para <Fase>. Para reabri-lo, clique aqui' and appends a Histórico entry. CORRECTED (Iteration 2, confirmed via Gerenciar > Configurações do pipe + its Atividades > Alterações de configuração log): card title is NOT hardcoded to the first start-form field — it is driven by an explicit 'Título do card' field-picker in Configurações do pipe (defaults to the first start-form field but is independently changeable at any time), the same title_field_id pattern as feature-005's Database Table records. The config-change log literally records 'Atualizou a configuração do título do card de "—" para "Nome do solicitante"'. CONFIRMED: a start-form field and a phase field with the identical label are separate Field rows with independent values — the clone must not merge/dedupe fields by label across owner types (start_form vs phase). Confirmed non-cloneable client quirk: phase column card-count badges do not live-update after a same-session move — only correct after a full reload; the clone should update counts synchronously instead.
data_model: cards: id, pipe_id (fk), phase_id (fk), title (derived live from pipe.title_field_id's value), done (bool), created_at, updated_at. card_field_values: id, card_id (fk), field_id (fk), value (text), filled_at. pipes gains: title_field_id (fk, nullable, defaults to the start form's first field)

description: Database Table entity — spreadsheet-like structured data object, separate from Pipes, with its own fields and records
page: Início > Databases tab (list) / /apollo_databases/:id (grid) / /apollo_databases/:id/records/:recordId (record detail) / /apollo_databases/:id/settings/general-settings (Configurações de database)
ui_details: Confirmed (Iteration 4, live test): 'Criar database' is a name-only modal, lands on an empty grid ('Título' column + 'Criar registro' FAB). Grid column '+' opens the same field-config modal shape as the Fases editor (Título do campo, Escolha o tipo, toggles, live preview, 'Dependências do campo' link) with a fuller palette than phases: Responsável, Anexo, Texto curto, Checkbox, Documentos, Moeda (nested currency-code sub-type e.g. 'USD - US Dollar'), Data, Data e hora, Data de vencimento, Email, ID, Etiquetas, Texto longo, Numérico, Número de telefone, Seleção de única opção, Seleção de lista, Texto fixo, Tempo, plus a 'Campos de conexão' group with only 'Conexão de database' (narrower than phase connectors, which can also target a pipe). The Formulário inicial settings tab additionally lists 'Conteúdo dinâmico' — a field type not seen in the Fases editor, not yet tested. 'Dependências do campo' is a read-only impact-analysis viewer ('Nenhuma dependência encontrada' + note that apps/integrations aren't listed), NOT a rule editor — unrelated to feature-009's Field Conditionals. Record creation modal lists only non-title fields (no separate Título input, unlike Cards); currency fields auto-mask raw digit input as cents ('15000' -> '$ 150.00' live). Record detail opens as a deep-linkable modal (icon+title, status badge w/ dropdown, 'Informações de registro' creator/timestamp, per-field hover-'Editar' inline edit w/ Salvar/Cancelar, 'Atualizado em' footer, '⋮' kebab with 'Editar campos'/'Deletar registro'). Configurações de database (Gerenciar) has: 'Título do registro' (dropdown choosing which field is the record's display title), 'Subtítulo do registro conectado' (default 'Criado em'), 'Texto do botão de criar registros' (default 'Criar registro'), 'Permissões' (Database público/privado radio), 'Autorizações' (checkbox: all members can create/edit/delete records), 'Excluir database'. Screenshots: screenshots/inspect/database-grid.jpg, screenshots/inspect/database-record-detail.jpg.
behavior: A Table has id (alphanumeric), name, public (bool), and table_fields (same type system as phase fields, richer palette per ui_details). A Table Record has id, title, and record_fields with rich per-type value columns (date_value, datetime_value, float_value, native_value, report_value). CONFIRMED: record title is NOT hardcoded to 'first field' — it's driven by an explicit title_field_id configured in Configurações de database, a real schema difference from Cards (whose title comes from the start form's first field and never re-derives). CONFIRMED client staleness quirk, same family as feature-004's Kanban count bug: saving a new field via '+' does not render the new column until reload (confirmed the save DID succeed server-side via a subsequent 'já está em uso' validation error on the label); a newly created record's own field values render as 'Vazio' and the 'N registros' header count doesn't update until reload either. CONFIRMED target-app bug (do not reproduce): the record detail modal's title-row status badge does not refresh after an inline field edit, persisting even across a fresh page navigation, while the field's own value and the grid row are both correct.
data_model: tables: id, org_id (fk), name, public (bool), title_field_id (fk, nullable), subtitle_template (text, default 'Criado em'), create_button_label (text, default 'Criar registro'), all_members_can_crud (bool). table_records: id, table_id (fk), title (derived live from title_field_id's value), created_at, updated_at. table_record_field_values: id, record_id (fk), field_id (fk), value (text), date_value, datetime_value, float_value

description: Automations engine: pipe-scoped trigger→action rules (10 trigger types × 12 action types), with a token/variable picker for dynamic values
ui_details: Confirmed (iteration 5, live test, created + fired a real rule): list view has search, Filtros, 'Ordenar por', a per-row on/off toggle, and a kebab (Editar/Duplicar/Excluir); empty state shows a two-icon diagram + 'Nova automação' CTA. The builder is a two-column 'Sempre que... / Faça isso...' picker. Triggers: 'Um card entrar em uma fase', 'Um campo for atualizado', 'Um card for criado', 'Uma atividade for recorrente', 'Um alerta for acionado', 'Um card sair de uma fase', 'Um email for recebido', 'Todos os cards conectados forem movidos para uma fase', 'Uma resposta for recebida da automação de requisição HTTP', 'Um botão em Interfaces é clicado'. Actions: 'Peça à IA', 'Envie uma tarefa', 'Mova um card', 'Atualize um campo no card ou registro', 'Crie um card ou registro conectado', 'Crie um card ou registro', 'Mova o card pai', 'Distribua responsáveis', 'Aplique uma fórmula', 'Faça uma requisição HTTP', 'Aplique regras de SLA', and 'Envie um template de email' (rendered greyed-out/disabled in this trial org — likely plan-gated). Selecting a trigger opens an inline config card (e.g. 'Um card entrar em uma fase' → pipe selector locked to current pipe + 'Para a fase' dropdown + '+ Adicionar condição'). Selecting an action opens its own inline config card (e.g. 'Atualize um campo no card ou registro' → 'Onde está o campo' radio [Pipe atual / Pipe ou database conectado] → warning banner about validating required-field references → 'Selecione um campo' dropdown → a value input with a '+' token-picker button). The token picker is a searchable dropdown grouped into 'Atributos de evento' (e.g. Data e Hora do evento), 'Atributos gerais' (Criado em, Fase atual, Data de vencimento, Finalizado em, ID, A última fase em que o card estava, Título), then one group PER PHASE NAME (e.g. 'Start form', 'Caixa de entrada') each listing that phase's own fields — inserted tokens render as removable pills. Saving prompts for a rule name via a small modal, then the rule appears in the list with an enabled toggle. Screenshot: screenshots/inspect/automations-builder.jpg.
behavior: CONFIRMED end-to-end: created a rule (trigger: card enters phase 'Fazendo' in this pipe; action: update the 'Caixa de entrada' phase's 'Nome do solicitante' field, value = a token for the start form's 'Nome do solicitante' field). Dragged a real card into 'Fazendo' — a toast confirmed the move, then Automações > Logs showed a new row (automation name, card name, card id, status 'Sucesso', start timestamp) within seconds, expandable to 'Automação executada com sucesso.' Opening the card's detail view and expanding its 'Caixa de entrada' Histórico entry confirmed the target field's value was actually written (previously blank, now 'João Silva'). KEY FINDING: the action's target field is NOT restricted to the trigger's destination phase — 'Fazendo' has zero fields configured, yet the rule successfully wrote to a field on a different phase entirely ('Caixa de entrada'). This means automation actions must be modeled as free field references across the whole pipe (any phase/start-form field, keyed by field id), not scoped to the triggering phase. description: Interfaces AI Assistant: a floating chat widget auto-mounted on every published/live Interfaces page, scoped to answer questions using that page's bound pipes/databases/documents
ui_details: CONFIRMED live iteration 6, discovered while testing feature-008 (Interfaces builder). A pill button ('AI Assistant', gradient purple/pink, sparkle icon) floats bottom-right on every published Interfaces page. On a viewer's FIRST visit to a given page it auto-expands to a full side panel (~500px wide, gradient background) with: header 'AI Assistant' + 'Beta' badge + overflow/expand/collapse controls; headline 'Encontre respostas e avance com suas solicitacoes'; 4 canned prompt chips (Ver minhas solicitacoes, Iniciar solicitacao, Resumir politicas e informacoes, Mostrar o que posso fazer aqui); a freeform 'Perguntar algo...' input with a send button; a footer disclaimer 'A IA pode cometer erros. Per project rules (no real multi-LLM orchestration), the clone should model this as a lightweight scoped Q&A stub: given the page's bound pipe/database schemas + record data, answer simple canned/templated queries (e.g. 'Ver minhas solicitacoes' -> filter the page's bound data tables to records assigned to the current viewer) rather than a general-purpose LLM chat.
data_model: No new persisted entity -- reads interface_page_elements for the current page (see feature-008's data model) to determine its answer scope. description: Meu trabalho ("My work") — org-level card assignment inbox: cards assigned to the current user across all pipes, filtered by due-date state, plus the notification system that surfaces overdue cards
ui_details: CONFIRMED live iteration 9. Header 'Meu trabalho' with subtitle 'Visualize e gerencie os cards atribuídos a você.' + a help-doc link. 6 filter tabs, each with a live count badge: 'Todos os cards', 'Cards prestes a vencer' (tooltip on hover: 'Cards que estão a 7 dias da data de vencimento'), 'Vencidos', 'Atrasados', 'Expirados', 'Concluídos'. Below the tabs, a sortable table (every column header is a sort button) with 6 columns: Título, Data de vencimento (renamed 'Vencidos em' while the Vencidos tab is active), Pipe, Fase atual, Criado em, Designado em. Standard pagination footer ('Anterior'/'Próximo', '1 - 1 de 1 resultados'). Empty state (shown per-tab, independently, even when other tabs have rows): 'Parece que ainda não há tarefas atribuídas a você. Que tal criar um card e atribuí-lo a si mesmo? Saiba mais.'
behavior: CONFIRMED live: assigned an existing card ('João Silva' in the Purchase Requests pipe) to the current user via the card detail's 'Adicionar responsável' control, then set its Vencimento (due date) to the previous day via the date-picker calendar (defaults to today's date/time when first opened). Both changes reflected on Meu trabalho within one page load: 'Todos os cards' and 'Vencidos' both went from 0 to 1, while 'Cards prestes a vencer' (due within 7 days but not yet passed) and 'Atrasados' stayed at 0 — confirming 'Vencidos' (due date already passed) and 'Atrasados' are DISTINCT states: Atrasados tracks phase/SLA time-in-phase expiration (the pipe-wide expiration alert from feature-014's Configurações do pipe), not the card's own Vencimento field. Each tab's empty state is independent — switching to a 0-count tab (e.g. 'Atrasados') shows the full empty-state block even though 'Todos os cards' has a row. The overdue transition auto-generated a real-time in-app notification ('O card "João Silva" está vencido') without any manual trigger — confirmed in both the header bell's popover (title 'Notificações', 'Marcar todas como lidas' link, unread items shown with a red badge count on the bell) and the dedicated /notifications page (each entry has a type-specific icon — a red overdue-clock glyph for this case — plus relative timestamp, e.g. 'há 2 minutos'). The bell's unread badge cleared automatically after visiting /notifications (read-state is a simple 'has the user opened the list' flag, not per-item until clicked). The top-right avatar button ('Conta e recursos', tied to the org's Tiago Vasconselos account) did not render a visible dropdown across 3 click attempts — account/profile management is explicitly out of scope per this project's spec, so not pursued further; the clone should still render the button as a stub even if it needs no working menu.
data_model: Meu trabalho is a computed, cross-pipe VIEW over the existing Card entity (feature-004) — no new persisted entity. Query: cards where assignee_ids CONTAINS current_user_id, joined to their pipe for the Pipe/Fase atual columns. Tab filters (computed booleans over the Card row, all relative to now()): 'Cards prestes a vencer' = due_date BETWEEN now() AND now()+7d; 'Vencidos' = due_date < now(); 'Atrasados' = phase_entered_at + phase.sla_duration < now() (references feature-014's per-phase SLA/expiration config, independent of due_date); 'Expirados' = a separate pipe-level expiration rule from Configurações do pipe firing; 'Concluídos' = card.phase.is_final (Concluído-type phase). Notification entity: id, user_id (fk), card_id (fk), type (enum, at least 'card_overdue'), message, created_at, read_at (nullable — set on any /notifications page visit, not per-item).

description: Pipe-scoped card search ("Procurar cards" box in the Kanban top nav) — client-side substring filter over already-loaded card titles, no server round-trip
ui_details: CONFIRMED live iteration 11. A single search input top-right of the Kanban phase-column strip, placeholder 'Procurar cards', with a search-glyph prefix icon and a clear ('x') button that appears once text is entered. A separate filter (funnel) icon sits immediately to its right — distinct control, not tested this pass. The search box has no dropdown/autocomplete affordance; it is a plain text input.
behavior: CONFIRMED live: typed 'João' into the box. Read `read_network_requests` immediately after — zero API/GraphQL calls fired (only an unrelated Intercom beacon), confirming the filter runs entirely client-side over cards already loaded into the Kanban board's in-memory state, not a server-side search endpoint. The filtered result did not appear instantly on keystroke: it applied a couple of seconds after the last keystroke (observed after pressing Return, but Return itself is not required — a follow-up screenshot with no Return press also showed the same debounce-then-filter behavior), consistent with a debounced client-side re-render rather than an Enter-triggered submit. Once applied, each phase column's card list is filtered independently by substring match against card title only (a 'Throwaway Test Card' did not match 'João' and was hidden; 'João Silva' did). The column's card-count badge updates to reflect the filtered count, and a phase with zero matches falls back to displaying that phase's normal empty-state copy (e.g. 'Aqui chegam os cards criados para este pipe') rather than a distinct 'no search results' message — the empty state is not search-aware. Clearing the box (the 'x' button) restores the full unfiltered board immediately.
data_model: No new entity — a pure client-side derived view. searchQuery: string (component-local UI state, not persisted, not part of the Card entity or any URL param observed). Filter predicate: card.title.toLowerCase().includes(searchQuery.toLowerCase()), applied independently within each phase's already-fetched card array.

description: Start form (Formulário inicial) editor as a dedicated deep-dive: the pipe's public card-intake form — internal builder view, public-facing branding customization ('Modo Público'), and start-form-specific Opções Avançadas
page: Gerenciar > Formulário inicial (/pipes/:id/settings/form); public-facing summary also surfaced at the pipe's own Formulário tab (/pipes/:id/form)
ui_details: CONFIRMED live iteration 11. The pipe-level 'Formulário' tab (distinct from the settings modal) shows a summary: a card-preview of the form, 'Visualizar'/'Editar' buttons, a live '{N} solicitações' counter with 'Ver no pipe' link, and a 'Próximos passos' tips panel (3 static suggestion cards: 'Habilite o rastreio de solicitações', 'Crie emails padronizados', 'Analise e exporte relatórios' — the latter two link to the Emails (feature-018) and Relatórios (feature-011) features respectively, confirming this panel is a cross-feature upsell surface, not a start-form-specific tool). Clicking 'Editar' opens the SAME 'Configurações do pipe' modal as Fases (feature-002) — tab 'Formulário inicial' is simply another tab alongside Fases/Pessoas/Email/Configurações do pipe, confirming the start form is modeled as phase-zero of the pipe rather than a separate entity. Within that tab: a top toggle between 'Editar formulário' (default) and 'Modo Público'. 'Editar formulário' reuses the identical field-type palette + per-field config side-panel already documented for Fases (feature-002/003) — same 23 field types, same toggles (Descrição/Texto de ajuda/obrigatório/Validação customizada/Visualização compacta/editável em outras fases/valor único), same 'Dependências do campo' link (feature-009's Condicionais). Distinct default for start-form fields: 'Este campo é editável em outras fases' defaults ON (phase fields default this OFF), since start-form answers typically need to stay editable downstream. 'Modo Público' is a start-form-exclusive sub-view not present on phase editors: a left config column (Editar logo — JPG/GIF/PNG, max 2MB; Título do formulário; Descrição do formulário; Texto do botão de envio, default 'Enviar'; Cor ou imagem de fundo; Cor da marca — a 10-swatch brand-color picker, same palette family as the pipe-icon-color picker from feature-014) and a live right-side preview of the actual public form exactly as an anonymous visitor sees it, including real legal/safety boilerplate ('Nunca envie senhas ou dados confidenciais...', 'Denunciar abuso', 'Termos e condições' links) and a 'Powered by Pipefy' footer badge. A separate top-level 'Opções Avançadas' link opens a small modal with 3 start-form-specific fields distinct from the public-mode fields: 'Título do formulário inicial' (the INTERNAL name shown on the Kanban/pipe nav, separate from the public-facing 'Título do formulário'), 'Texto do botão de criar cards' (default 'Criar novo card' — the internal submit-button label, distinct from the public form's 'Texto do botão de envio'/'Enviar'), and 'Título do card' (a field-picker dropdown selecting which start-form field drives card.title — same mechanism independently confirmed in feature-014's Configurações do pipe general settings).
behavior: CONFIRMED live: added a new required 'Texto curto' field ('Departamento') via the field-type palette — it inserted instantly with an autosave toast ('Configurações atualizadas.') and no explicit Save click needed, appearing simultaneously in the internal preview, the public Formulário tab summary, and the 'Modo Público' live preview. Toggling to 'Modo Público' requires an explicit 'Salvar' click per the visual design (Salvar button present, greyed until a change is made) — unlike the field-palette side, which autosaves per-field. Opções Avançadas is a True separate save action ('Salvar opções' button) scoped only to its own 3 fields.
data_model: StartForm is not a separate entity — it is Phase id=0 (or a phase-like row flagged is_start_form=True) of the Pipe's ordered Phase list (feature-002), sharing the Field entity/type system (feature-003) and Field Conditionals (feature-009). Additional start-form-only attributes beyond the base Phase model: public_title (string, shown to anonymous visitors, defaults to pipe name), public_description (text, nullable), public_logo (nullable file ref, JPG/GIF/PNG ≤2MB), public_submit_button_text (string, default 'Enviar'), public_background (color hex or image ref), public_brand_color (enum from the shared 10-color pipe palette), internal_title (string, shown on the pipe's internal nav, defaults to pipe name — distinct from public_title), internal_create_button_text (string, default 'Criar novo card'), title_field_id (fk to a Field on this phase, drives card.title — same mechanism as feature-014).
